public_comment.topic: Urged the committee to add all other likely upcoming capital costs to the price tag before going to voters, since residents vote their pocketbooks.

votes.outcome: passed (7 audible yes votes; Greg's vote not audible)

budget_items.what_was_said: A roughly $300,000 item for repairing the TC Pacios roof appeared at a special town meeting; members questioned whether to repair it or tear down parts of the building instead.
Tony called it a mistake to bring a $22 million town administrative project to voters the same night as the Marshall Park vote, without any stated priority between them.

budget_items.topic: Future capital price tag for town admin project
budget_items.what_was_said: Tony suggested the town could still sell a town administration project even at a $10 million price tag if it is framed as the first piece of a longer capital plan.

budget_items.topic: Hypothetical combined cost of all major capital projects
budget_items.what_was_said: Tony said totaling every major capital project (town admin, Marshall Park, Turkey Hill, Brooks House, etc.) at once could reach $150 million, which would be unsellable to voters without prioritization.

budget_items.topic: Range of possible borrowing for combined projects
budget_items.what_was_said: Dave, referencing Tony's point, said the borrowing being discussed across projects could be 150 million, maybe 100 million, or maybe 75, without settling on a figure.
Tony noted the capital improvements committee spends an incredible amount of time each year deciding how to allocate about $2 million in town capital money.

Dave repeated the roughly $2 million a year capital improvements figure while arguing the town has never built a priority list for its much larger construction projects; he noted he was making the number up as an approximation.

budget_items.topic: Debt capacity for the building project
budget_items.what_was_said: Tom, for the finance committee, said the town has plenty of room within its debt limits for this project, pending what happens with Turkey Hill and other building renovations.

budget_items.topic: Finance committee review of prior plan's debt impact
budget_items.what_was_said: Tom said the finance committee went back through the numbers on the original roughly 22 million plan plus the park plan and Turkey Hill work with assumed interest rates and terms, and concluded the debt percentages would be fine.
Matt said capital planning has long held that the Brooks House needs a lot of money to remain usable, and he worried the cost may make it impractical despite its value for the ACE program.
Tom recalled decade-old task force estimates for Brooks House work were already substantial and said they could now be two to four times higher due to inflation.

minutes.headline: Committee elects new chair, narrows scope to town hall/Ritter/Brooks House, and pushes for a town-wide capital priority list
minutes.summary: A reconstituted Municipal Building Design Committee elected a chair and vice chair, then reset its charter after a prior building project failed at the ballot: the plan now focuses on renovating Ritter/town hall and rehousing PAC and ACE (in the Brooks House) rather than building new space in town hall. Members agreed to interview town departments directly, tour other town halls, and pressed the select board/master plan process for a town-wide capital project priority list before returning to voters, setting the next meeting for September 29th.

what_happened.line: The committee reset its charter to renovating town hall/Ritter and moving PAC and ACE out of town hall into the Brooks House, dropping the earlier new-construction plan that failed at the ballot.
Members elected Dave Blad as chair and Tony as vice chair, both by unanimous votes.
Several members pushed for a town-wide capital project priority list, citing a wide range of figures for what combined major projects could cost, before any plan goes back to voters.
The committee plans to interview town departments directly, tour other town halls, and set its next meeting for September 29.

why_it_matters: Any renovation of town hall/Ritter or relocation of PAC and ACE into the Brooks House will eventually come back to residents as a debt-financed building project.
How this project is ranked against other large capital items, such as Turkey Hill and Marshall Park, will shape how much residents are asked to approve and when.
